one_liner: Callback-driven C Markdown-to-HTML library (Sundown fork); edged out cmark 0.21 s vs 0.29 s in cmark's own 2015-era benchmark.
what_it_does: Renders original Markdown 1.0 (plus optional extensions: tables, fenced code, footnotes, autolinks, strikethrough, underline, highlight, quote, superscript, math) to HTML or a table of contents. You create a renderer (hoedown_html_renderer_new), a document (hoedown_document_new with extension flags and a max nesting depth) and call hoedown_document_render into a hoedown_buffer. The parser is decoupled from output through a struct of renderer callbacks, so custom output formats are written by filling in callbacks; it is not API- or output-compatible with cmark.
how_it_is_fast: There is no AST: a first pass strips reference definitions into a small hash table and expands tabs into one buffer, then a recursive-descent block parser calls renderer callbacks that append straight to the output buffer. Inline parsing copies runs of ordinary bytes in bulk and dispatches only on 'active' characters through a 256-entry lookup table into a function-pointer array. Temporary buffers come from per-document pooled stacks reused across nesting levels, and the output buffer is pre-grown to 1.5x the input, so allocation is rare; the Makefile builds with -O3.
when_to_use: Rendering trusted Markdown (your own docs or sites) in C or C++ where throughput matters and CommonMark conformance does not.
Keeping output compatible with existing Sundown or Redcarpet-family renderers and their extension set.
Custom output formats or streaming HTML with low memory, using the renderer callback struct instead of walking an AST.
Dependency-free embedding under ISC on GCC, Clang or MSVC (Makefile.win provided).
when_not_to_use: When CommonMark or GFM conformance is required: it targets the Markdown 1.0.x test suites, CommonMark support was never added (issue #119 open), and cmark's why-cmark-and-not-x.md lists list-nesting, heading, reference and title-escaping bugs as of v3.0.3.
Untrusted input on a server: 50,000 nested brackets took 17.84 s (cmark 0.073 s), and 160,000 reference definitions with 10,000 references took 8.78 s (open issue #223); out-of-memory calls abort().
Pages that need link sanitizing: the HTML renderer percent-escapes hrefs but does not filter schemes, so javascript: links pass through even with HOEDOWN_HTML_ESCAPE.
Non-ASCII text that relies on Unicode case folding or punctuation: reference labels are folded with byte-wise tolower and non-ASCII punctuation and whitespace count as word characters.
Projects that need a maintained dependency: last commit 2015-12-07 (version 3.0.7).

integration.form: source-drop (9 .c files in src/; make also builds libhoedown.a and libhoedown.so)
integration.min_toolchain: C99 per README (the Makefile compiles with -O3 -ansi -pedantic); MSVC via Makefile.win, with buffer.h stubbing __attribute__ and __builtin_expect
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. Parse state (reference table, work-buffer pools) lives in the hoedown_document and TOC state in the renderer, so use one document and renderer per thread.

gotchas: Reference links are matched by a 32-bit sdbm-style hash only: struct link_ref stores no label and find_link_ref returns the first entry whose hash matches, so two different labels with equal hashes resolve to the same URL, and a reference to an undefined label can silently link to another definition. Computing the same hash in Python found colliding 10-character labels ('f3yy839674' and 'bpnm1bsoj2') after about 150,000 random tries (hash computed, not run through hoedown). Footnotes use the same hash-only id.
The reference table has only 8 buckets (REF_TABLE_SIZE 8), so lookups degrade to linear chain scans on documents with many references, which is the cause behind the 8.78 s case in issue #223.
Anything nested deeper than max_nesting (the CLI default is 16) is silently dropped: parse_block and parse_inline return without emitting the text.
hoedown_buffer grows by a fixed unit (arithmetic, not geometric growth); give large documents a large unit or pre-grow the buffer to avoid repeated reallocs.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: MD4C is the catalogued Markdown sibling: it is CommonMark-compliant, still maintained and itself measured 1.4-7.7x faster than cmark, so prefer it by default; pick hoedown only to keep Sundown/Redcarpet-style output or its bundled SmartyPants and TOC renderer on trusted input.
verified_claims_summary: cmark's benchmarks.md (tags 0.21.0 to 0.29.0) times each CLI on an 11 MB concatenation of all Pro Git first-edition translations on a 2 GHz Core 2 Duo laptop with time -p (0.01 s resolution), subtracting an empty-input run and taking the median of 10: hoedown 0.21 s vs cmark 0.29 s (about 1.4x, derived from page data) and discount 1.85 s. No compiler, flags or hoedown version are given, the hoedown binary presumably ran with its CLI defaults (no extensions, max nesting 16), and the two programs implement different Markdown dialects, so the outputs being timed are not the same.
status_note: Abandoned since 2015-12-07 at version 3.0.7; ISC-licensed and small enough to vendor, but the hash-only reference matching, the open many-references slowdown (#223) and the lack of URL scheme filtering make it a poor fit for untrusted input.
